structure: Part 1, Service-wide rows. Read the backlog's top level (run_id EUDPA-328-DR1U, target live-animals-frontend, corpus dr1u, 161 increments) and six service-wide rows in full by line range: inc-003 phase banner (lines 4-155, done, notes with CORRECTION 1-2, a RULING on the feedback link, VERIFIED BEFORE BUILD, NOT AVAILABLE, BLAST RADIUS, RELATED; one openQuestion), inc-004 section caption above headings (156-338, done, one openQuestion on caption placement), inc-007 service navigation items (507-676, done, three openQuestions: tests-repo auth specs, visual baseline, orphaned view-context fields), inc-161 what a page offers at its foot (4240-5105, done, decision accept: rule (b), with the verifier's notes on which pages keep the controls), inc-006 save and cancel controls (7174-7344, done, two dated notes) and inc-013 save-and-return button and cancel link on five pages (31606-31729, dropped, decision reject). Claims cover every RULING, decision, note and open question in those rows, plus what each done row settled where the row's own difference states a choice the later DR2.1 work must weigh (banner copy, caption set and exclusions, navigation items and hrefs, the hub-to-overview rename, the rule (b) page list, which pages keep the controls, and the mechanism). Provenance notes, PR and commit bookkeeping, evidence, screens and the verifier's count corrections were read for context and not claimed, except where a provenance note records the ruling itself.

claims.statement: DR1 judged that Design release 1 states no rule for which pages carry the return controls, and that its single-button pages are omissions rather than decisions, so its page-by-page pattern is not copied.
claims.quote: The design's own routing says the single-button pages are omissions rather than decisions.

claims.statement: Whatever the rule, check your answers and the declaration keep a lone "Continue", and the delete-notification and cancel-amendment confirmation pages keep their confirm-or-go-back endings.

claims.statement: Rule (b) changes no control's wording; it changes only which pages render the return controls. The primary's wording and the return controls' wording are owned by other rows.
claims.quote: This finding changes no string at all; it changes which pages render the controls

claims.statement: Design release 1's extra cancel destinations ("Cancel and return to dashboard" on the transporter forms, "Cancel and return to address book") were not adopted: rule (b) changes no wording and keeps one cancel destination, the overview.
claims.quote: the cancel control has three destinations rather than one — "Cancel and return to overview" as a link on the 29, "Cancel and return to dashboard" as a secondary button on three, and "Cancel and return to address book" as a secondary button on three
claims.note: Inferred from the ruling naming no new destination and the finding stating that nothing changes what any control says.

claims.statement: Design release 1 lays the two buttons on a row with the cancel link in a paragraph beneath, where the frontend puts all three on one line; the row records this layout difference without a ruling on it.
claims.quote: One arrangement difference runs through all 29: Design release 1 puts the two buttons on a row and the cancel link in a paragraph beneath them, where the frontend puts all three on one line.
claims.note: Neither the decision nor the difference says whether the layout should change.

claims.statement: Under rule (b) the first page of each task row, the page the overview links to, keeps all three controls; so origin and contact keep their return controls even though Design release 1 ends origin-of-the-import with a lone "Save and continue" and contact-address-for-consignment with a bare "Continue".
claims.quote: Only the pages the overview links to end with the three controls; a page reached from another page ends with the primary alone.
